datasets.title: Kiribati: High Resolution Population Density Maps + Demographic Estimates
datasets.description: The world's most accurate population datasets. Seven maps/datasets for the distribution of various populations in Kiribati: (1) Overall population density (2) Women (3) Men (4) Children (ages 0-5) (5) Youth (ages 15-24) (6) Elderly (ages 60+) (7) Women of reproductive age (ages 15-49).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/kiribati-high-resolution-population-density-maps-demographic-estimates]
datasets.details: To reference this data, please use the following citation: Facebook Connectivity Lab and Center for International Earth Science Information Network - CIESIN - Columbia University. 2016. High Resolution Settlement Layer (HRSL). Source imagery for HRSL © 2016 DigitalGlobe. Accessed DAY MONTH YEAR.' Please note that as of 2024, Meta's high resolution population density maps are no longer being updated.

entity.name: AI and Data for Good at Meta (Facebook)

lineage.description: Building footprints were extracted from commercial satellite imagery using machine learning techniques developed by Meta. These footprints were combined with national census data and demographic statistics in partnership with Columbia University to produce high-resolution gridded population density maps disaggregated by age and sex groups. The resulting datasets support disaster risk assessments by providing spatially explicit exposure estimates for vulnerable population subgroups in Kiribati.

sources.name: AI and Data for Good at Meta (Facebook)
sources.description: Machine learning models applied to commercially available satellite imagery to identify building footprints, used as the spatial basis for disaggregating population estimates.

sources.name: Columbia University
sources.description: Provides population disaggregation methodology overlaying general population estimates from publicly available census data onto the building footprint layer.
